targets.evidence_quote: Using a pre-registered replication of Burden (2008), we do not find consistent evidence that changes in the wording of the partisanship question can significantly alter the size of the partisan gender gap.
targets.outcome_quote: Contrary to Burden (2008), our data show that measures of partisanship that prime affect do not lead women to be more likely to identify as Republicans. Rather, these measures lead women of both parties to be more likely to identify as independent—a pattern that leaves the partisan gender gap in place, but suggests that both parties may be losing women.
